But IMO Denver holds all the chips. If the 'Cos franchise tag Miller this year they only have to pay him about $14 million vs the nearly $20 million they're offering. Even if they had to tag him for the next three years they never would get to the nearly $20 million that's on the table. By the time they couldn't tag him further he'd be 30 and his best years behind him. That's not to say three years from now he'll be a scrub, but he might not be worth the nearly $20 million a year they're offering at this point.

Certainly Miller could sit out this year if tagged. But it'd be a huge gamble on his part. Do you want to sit out a year in the prime of your career, in the prime of your earning potential? Do you want to walk away from $14 million when you're an off the field weight room accident away from never seeing another penny? Denver can probably afford to play the blinking contest. Coming off a Super Bowl win with Peyton retiring and a rookie QB as the theoretical future of the team their fan base, which is used to winning but also isn't unreasonable, can probably be placated to "trust the process" if they aren't a real contender this year. It helps that John Elway is the Duke of Denver and his presence is larger in that town than maybe any other sports icon in any other city. He gave them Super Bowls on the field, and now he's given them Super Bowls from behind the desk. If he tells those fans upping his offer to Miller isn't worth it they will believe him. Even if the vibe going into the July 15 deadline was Miller might sit you can bet he'd just be hit with the non-exclusive version of the tag so if he signed with someone else Elway with his great draft record would just pick up two first round picks, thank you very much.
